area: Employee job TITLE and WAGE derivation from skill (for native Filiaalmanager / Team Leader roles)
findings:
=== 1. WHERE THE "JOB TITLE" COMES FROM ===

There is NO job-title field anywhere. `BigAmbitions.Characters.Skills.SkillData` (BigAmbitions.Characters/BigAmbitions.Characters.decompiled.cs:618-641) has fields: `skillName`, `baseHourlyWage`, `trainingCostMultiplier`, `secondarySkill`, `secondarySkillRange` (Vector2Int default 5-20), `icon28` (Sprite), `associatedColorGradient` (Gradient), `possibleDealbreakers` (List<string>). It extends `TaggedScriptableObject`. No name/title/nameKey/localizationKey member.

The displayed "job title" is ALWAYS the employee's primary-skill NAME STRING resolved through the Localizor localization system, where **the localization key IS the exact skill-name string** (e.g. `"ba:skill_purchasingagent"`). Proof: `Tutorial/QuestEntryCustomLocalizationFromSkillName.GetLocalization` (line 33-40) does `label = BusinessTypeHelper.GetData(...).employeePrimarySkills[0]; ... skillName = label.GetLocalization()` — a raw skill id passed straight into `.GetLocalization()`. Same in `Helpers/LocalizationHelper.cs` idiom and `UI.Smartphone.Apps.Shared.BaseEmployeeModel..ctor` (BaseEmployeeModel.cs:35): `primarySkill = primarySkillName.GetLocalization() + $"{primarySkillPercentage:000}"`.

`Entities.EmployeeInstance.GetPrimarySkill()` (EmployeeInstance.cs:238-241) = `characterData.skills.First().name`. So the FIRST skill in the list is the role. `Helpers.EmployeeHelper.CreateAIEmployeeInstance` and `Helpers.RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate` both add the role skill first.

Enumerated display paths that render the skill as a title/label:
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.Shared.BaseEmployeeModel..ctor` BaseEmployeeModel.cs:35 — builds the sort/search string via `primarySkillName.GetLocalization()`. Feeds EmployeeModel, CandidateModel, ScheduleEmployeeModel, HrManagerEmployeeModel.
- `EmployeeCellView.SetData` (root namespace) EmployeeCellView.cs:59-63 — My Employees list row. `primarySkill` is a `TextLocalizationComponent`; `.Arguments = new { skillName = data.primarySkillName, percentage = data.primarySkillPercentage }` (raw skill id passed as arg; the component's Key is set in the prefab).
- `CandidateCellView.SetData` (root namespace) CandidateCellView.cs:62-66 — My Employees > Candidates list row. Same `{ skillName = data.primarySkillName, percentage }` pattern.
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.MyEmployees.MyEmployees.ShowEmployee` MyEmployees.cs:361-365 — the employee DETAIL CARD skill rows: `obj.GetLanguageChangeEventByName("SkillName").Key = skill.name;` (raw skill id used directly as the Localizor key), `SkillLevel` text = `skill.GetRoundedValue() + "%"`.
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HRManagers.EmployeeCellView.SetData` BigAmbitions/UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.HrManagers/EmployeeCellView.cs:45-52 — the HQ manager-plan employee cell (the template the new HQ tabs will clone): `primarySkill.Arguments = new { skill = data.primarySkillName, value = ... }`.
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.Schedule.ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox.SetUpSkill` ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox.cs:50-62 — BizMan Schedule skill chip: `label.Key = "employees_skill_with_percentage"`, `label.Arguments = new { skillName = skill.name.GetLocalization(), percentage = skill.GetRoundedValue() }` (here the id is PRE-resolved before being passed).
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.Shared.EmployeeFilterToggleBase.ConfigureSkill` EmployeeFilterToggleBase.cs:18-23 — filter chip label: `label.Key = skill` (raw id).
- `Entities.EmployeeInstance.GetEmployeeNameWithInfo` EmployeeInstance.cs:206-212 — `"employee_name_with_skill".Localize(new { name, skillValue = <number> })` — uses only the numeric skill value, NOT the skill name; not a title path.
- Recruitment/headhunter/training text messages pass the raw skill id as data (e.g. `RecruitmentAgencyDialog.OnRecruitmentSettingsSet` RecruitmentAgencyDialog.cs:211 `{ "skillKey", skillName }`; `EmployeeHelper.ShowFinishedTrainingEmployeeNotifications` line 304 `dictionary.Add("skill", <skill name>)`).

Conclusion for the mod: provide a Localizor table entry keyed by the exact skill id → "Filiaalmanager" / "Team Leader". Both raw-id and pre-resolved arg paths then render correctly.

=== 2. THE WAGE FORMULA ===

`Helpers.EmployeeHelper.CalculateHourlyWageForSkill(Skill skill)` and the overload `(string skillName, float skillValue)` — EmployeeHelper.cs:351-365:

  wage = SkillHelper.GetData(skill).baseHourlyWage
       * GetSkillWageBoost(skillValue)
       * SaveGameManager.Current.gameVariables.employeeHourlySalaryMultiplier

`Helpers.EmployeeHelper.GetSkillWageBoost(float skillValue)` EmployeeHelper.cs:367-370:
  return Mathf.Pow(skillValue, 1.05f) / 100f + 1f;

`employeeHourlySalaryMultiplier` = 1.0 by default (GameVariables.cs:27); difficulty slider range 0.5–1.3 (DifficultySetting.cs:26-27).

Boost factor by skill value: v=20 → ~1.23; v=50 → ~1.61; v=75 → ~1.93; v=100 → ~2.26.

The ONLY SkillData field feeding wage is `baseHourlyWage` (float). So `SkillData.baseHourlyWage` alone sets the ladder position; skill value and difficulty are multipliers on top.

Where the employee's stored `EmployeeInstance.hourlyWage` (EmployeeInstance.cs:65) is assigned from it:
- `Helpers.RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate` RecruitmentHelper.cs:78 — `hourlyWage = CalculateHourlyWageForSkill(skills.First())` at generation.
- `Buildings.BuildingTypes.Shared.AiBusinessEmployeeData.GetEmployeeInstance` AiBusinessEmployeeData.cs:110 — rival employees.
- `Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes.CompatibilityFixesEA05.FixTooLowSalariesInOldSaveGames` line 20 — save repair (× 0.5).
- `Buildings.Office.Headquarters.HeadhunterPlan.GetWageRangeForSkill` HeadhunterPlan.cs:80-82 — shows the min/max wage band in the headhunter UI.
- `Helpers.EstimatedWeeklyIncomeHelper.CalculateWeeklyWages` EstimatedWeeklyIncomeHelper.cs:197 — projected P&L.
- After hire, training raises it: `EmployeeInstance.IncreaseWageFromTraining` EmployeeInstance.cs:293-301 scales `hourlyWage` by `pow(GetSkillWageBoost(new)/GetSkillWageBoost(old), 0.7)` for the primary skill.

Recruitment-agency campaign candidates arrive at skill value 20 (`RecruitmentAgencyDialog.OnRecruitmentSettingsSet` RecruitmentAgencyDialog.cs:170 `percentage = 20f`); headhunter candidates use the target-slider value. For a standard (non-rival, non-poached) hire the negotiation does NOT inflate: `AI.Employees.SalaryNegotiation.CandidateSalaryNegotiation.GetInitialOffer` CandidateSalaryNegotiation.cs:85-96 returns `employeeInstance.hourlyWage` unchanged (only `Mathf.Ceil(w*20)/20` rounding).

To calibrate against the target ($16/hr store employee, ~$30/hr Store Manager): at skill 20, baseHourlyWage ≈ target / 1.23; at skill 50, ≈ target / 1.61. So roughly base ≈ 10-13 for a store employee skill, ≈ 18-24 for the Store Manager skill, ≈ 14-18 for Team Leader — final numbers need a runtime dump of shipped skills' baseHourlyWage to sit correctly in the existing ladder.

Wage display fields (all read `EmployeeInstance.hourlyWage`, format `.ToCurrencyFormat()`):
- `MyEmployees.ShowEmployee` MyEmployees.cs:337-340 (detail card, key `common_hourly_wage`)
- `EmployeeCellView` EmployeeCellView.cs:58, `CandidateCellView` CandidateCellView.cs:61
- BizMan/HrManagers `EmployeeCellView` cs:53-58 (key arg `wage`), `HrManagerPlanUI` cs:137 (avg), `ScheduleEmployeeCellView` cs:125-128
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.Contacts.ContactsApp` cs:792 (salary-negotiation message)

=== 3. UI SPOTS THAT NPE WITHOUT A REAL SkillData (or a Harmony guard) ===

`SkillHelper.GetData(string)` / `GetData(Skill)` (BigAmbitions.Characters.decompiled.cs:661-669) = `Skills.GetValueOrDefault(name)` → returns **null** on miss (no throw at the lookup; callers dereference and NRE). `SkillHelper.Skills` is (re)built only by `OnSkillDataLoaded`, wired via `BigAmbitions.SaveSystem.AddressableLoader` line 170: `Register<SkillData>("Skills", SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded)` — reloaded on each city load, so mod skills must be re-injected each load.

HARD CRASH — unguarded `SkillHelper.GetData(x).<member>`:
- Helpers/EmployeeHelper.cs:353 and :361 — `.baseHourlyWage` (every hire, candidate-gen, wage estimate, headhunter band)
- Helpers/EmployeeHelper.cs:452-453 — `GetTrainingCost` `.trainingCostMultiplier`
- Helpers/RecruitmentHelper.cs:65-66 — `GenerateCandidate` `.secondarySkill`
- Buildings.BuildingTypes.Shared/AiBusinessEmployeeData.cs:98-104 — `.secondarySkill`, `.secondarySkillRange` (rival businesses only)
- Buildings.Office.Headquarters/HeadhunterPlan.cs:74-78 (`GetWageRangeForSkill`), :108 (`CheckForRecruiting`), :138-139 (`GetRandomDemandsForCandidate` `.secondarySkill`, `.HasTag`)
- Entities.Employee.JobDemands/JobDemandHelper.cs:124 (`GetIdealNumberOfDemands`), :142-143 (`GetRandomHoursPerWeekDemandForSkill`) — `.HasTag`; reached by `EmployeeInstance.GenerateDemands`/`GetIdealNumberOfDemands` (EmployeeInstance.cs:647,663,694,713) on EVERY candidate generated
- Helpers/RecruitmentCommands.cs:30 — debug console `Command_GenerateCandidate` `.HasTag`
- UI.Dialog/RecruitmentSettings.cs:126 — `SelectSkill` `.HasTag` (recruitment agency dropdown)
- Dialogs/RecruitmentAgencyDialog.cs:158 — `OnRecruitmentSettingsSet` `.HasTag`
- UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.Schedule/ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox.cs:60 — `.icon28` (store schedule skill chip)
- UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.Schedule/ScheduleHelper.cs:142 — `GetEmployeeColor` `.associatedColorGradient` (store schedule row bg + WorkShiftSlider.cs:101 + ScheduleEmployeeScrollerController.cs:99)
- Helpers/EstimatedWeeklyIncomeHelper.cs:197 — via CalculateHourlyWageForSkill
- Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes: EnsureAllFullTimeEmployeesHaveFullTimeDemand.cs:14,21; EnablePartAndFullTimeToRecruitmentCampaigns.cs:13 — `.HasTag` during save-load migration

The two Schedule paths (ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox.cs:60, ScheduleHelper.cs:142) are only reached if the role is assignable to a store WORK SHIFT / workstation. `ba:skill_purchasingagent` and the manager skills are NOT (they are HQ-plan roles), so `ScheduleEmployeeScrollerController` never builds a ScheduleEmployeeModel for them — if the new roles follow the Purchasing-Agent model these two are effectively dead paths. All the wage/demand paths above ARE hit on every generation/hire regardless.

NULL-SAFE (won't crash even if GetData returns null):
- Entities/EmployeeInstance.cs:230, :235 — `HasAnySkillWithTag`: `characterData.skills.Select(x => SkillHelper.GetData(x.name)).Any(x => x?.HasTag(tag) ?? true)` (null → treated as true)
- Buildings.Office.Headquarters/HeadhunterHelper.cs:100-101 — explicit `if (data == null || ...)` guard
- UI.Smartphone.Apps.MyEmployees/EmployeeFilterController.cs:14 and CandidateFilterController.cs:14 — explicit `!(SkillHelper.GetData(skill) == null)` guard: a registered skill gets a filter chip, an unregistered one is silently skipped

Tolerates a null/placeholder Sprite/Gradient once GetData returns a valid SkillData object (does NOT crash):
- ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox.cs:60 `iconImage.sprite = ...icon28` — Unity `Image` with a null sprite just renders nothing
- ScheduleHelper.cs:142 gradient `.EvaluateRandom(...)` — a default `new Gradient()` still returns a color
- Every name/label path (`TextLocalizationComponent`, `GetLanguageChangeEventByName(...).Key`, filter `label.Key`) never touches SkillData; a missing Localizor key only shows the raw key text, no exception

So a mod-supplied (or Harmony-synthesized) SkillData that fills `baseHourlyWage`, a non-null `icon28`, a non-null `associatedColorGradient`, and the right `TagRef.Skilltag` tags eliminates every crash path.

=== 4. LOCALIZATION KEY FORMATION ===

The skill display-name key = the raw skill-name string verbatim (no prefix/suffix transform), e.g. `"ba:skill_purchasingagent"`, `"ba:skill_cleaning"`. `.GetLocalization()` (extension on string, from the third-party `Localizor` asset — not in the decomp) and `TextLocalizationComponent` / `LanguageChangeEventDataHolder` all take that string as the key. Standard Localizor miss behavior is to echo the key text (so a missing entry shows "sm:skill_storemanager", never a crash).

Mod locale injection is supported by the loader: `BigAmbitions.ModsInternal.ModLifecycleLoader` calls `LocalizorManager.LoadLocalizationTables(reloadIndex: false)` after every mod load/unload (ModLifecycleLoader.cs:88, :127, :160). So a localization table bundled with the mod (keyed `sm:skill_storemanager` → "Filiaalmanager", `sm:skill_teamleader` → "Team Leader", plus any `_description` keys and the `employees_skill_with_percentage`-style templates if you introduce new ones) is picked up automatically. Also localize the training/notification helper keys if the roles are trainable.

=== 5. DOES MY EMPLOYEES FILTER / GROUP BY SKILL VIA A HARD-CODED SWITCH? ===

No. `UI.Smartphone.Apps.MyEmployees.EmployeeFilterController.CreateToggles` (EmployeeFilterController.cs:10-21) and `CandidateFilterController` iterate `SkillHelper.AllSkillNames` and create one toggle per non-null skill. `UI.Smartphone.Apps.Shared.EmployeeFilterToggleBase.ConfigureSkill` sets `label.Key = skill`; `ShouldKeep` (EmployeeFilterToggleBase.cs:44-47) matches `employee.primarySkillName == _skill`. A registered mod skill auto-appears as a filter chip with the localized label; nothing to patch. No skill-based grouping or sort toggle exists in `MyEmployees` / `EmployeeScrollerController` / the sort toggles.

The ONE hard-coded skill switch in the hire path is `Helpers.RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate` (RecruitmentHelper.cs:43-50):
  skillName switch {
    "ba:skill_logisticsmanager" => new LogisticsManager(),
    "ba:skill_hrmanager"        => new HRManager(),
    "ba:skill_headhunter"       => new Headhunter(),
    "ba:skill_pricingmanager"   => new PricingManager(),
    _ => new EmployeeInstance() }
A new skill falls to `new EmployeeInstance()` — exactly like `ba:skill_purchasingagent`, which is also absent from this switch. Those subclasses (Entities/LogisticsManager.cs etc.) only override `Reset()` / `UnAssignWork()` to detach their HQ plan on fire/reset. If you want that auto-cleanup for Filiaalmanager / Team Leader you must Harmony-patch this switch (and `AiBusinessEmployeeData` / poaching if the skill is ever added to `BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills`); otherwise plain `EmployeeInstance` is functionally fine and the mod's own plan code handles unassignment.

feasibility: Native title+wage is fully data-driven and achievable, BUT it hard-requires a real (or Harmony-synthesized) SkillData object registered in SkillHelper.Skills for each new skill. Title = a Localizor table entry keyed by the exact skill id (mod ships a locale table; loader re-loads it via LocalizorManager.LoadLocalizationTables). Wage ladder position = SkillData.baseHourlyWage (final wage = baseHourlyWage * (pow(skillValue,1.05)/100+1) * difficultyMultiplier). Needs asset bundle (a SkillData ScriptableObject under Addressables label "Skills") OR — more robust given mod skills are wiped on each city load — a Harmony postfix on SkillHelper.GetData plus SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded that injects a synthetic SkillData with baseHourlyWage, non-null icon28, non-null associatedColorGradient, and the correct TagRef.Skilltag tags set. With that object present, all ~15 unguarded GetData(...).member call sites (wage calc, training cost, GenerateCandidate, JobDemandHelper on every candidate, HeadhunterPlan, RecruitmentSettings, schedule icon/color) stop crashing. The RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate skill->subclass switch degrades gracefully to plain EmployeeInstance (identical to ba:skill_purchasingagent); Harmony-patch it only if you want the subclass Reset()/UnAssignWork() plan-cleanup hooks. My Employees filtering is dynamic and needs no patch.
